question: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (Allen et al., 1998), Chapter 4, Example 18, computes the daily reference evapotranspiration for Brussels (50 degrees 48 minutes N, 100 m above sea level) on 6 July from: maximum and minimum air temperature 21.5 and 12.3 degrees C, maximum and minimum relative humidity 84 and 63 percent, wind speed 10 km/h measured at 10 m height, and 9.25 hours of bright sunshine; the worked example derives an incoming solar radiation of 22.07 and a net radiation of 13.28 MJ m-2 per day from the sunshine hours, with soil heat flux taken as zero. Compute ET0 for that day with each of the six formulations the registered pyet model offers, using every input each formulation is entitled to and converting units and measurement height where needed. Then sweep the daily mean air temperature from 12.9 to 20.9 degrees C in 1 degree steps, holding the other inputs, and plot all six formulations on one chart. Compare the Penman-Monteith value at the example's mean temperature with the value FAO-56 publishes for Example 18, if you can establish it, and explain why the formulations disagree.
